items.text: Request, feature, preprocessing, model, and decision-policy versions are compatible and traceable.
Quality and performance are measured on target hardware with representative shapes and concurrency.
The latency and availability SLO covers feature lookup, queueing, inference, policy, and network time.
Load tests identify saturation, batch limits, memory headroom, and autoscaling lag.
Prediction and exposure records can join to delayed outcomes by model version and cohort.
Deadlines propagate through dependencies and timed-out work is cancelled.
Admission control and load shedding protect critical traffic before queues become unbounded.
Each decision class has a tested fallback, abstention, or human-review policy.
Canary guardrails include model quality and safety signals as well as service health.
The previous artifact and its feature contract remain available for a rapid rollback.
